hypothesis: On FreeBSD x86-64, building the GLM engine with clang (the base system's compiler, LLVM libomp, with KMP_BLOCKTIME=0 so idle threads sleep at once) decodes GLM-5.3 faster than building it with gcc (libgomp), with identical output.
model: GLM-5.3 (744B MoE, 419 GB on disk), colibri int8 container, experts and dense at 8 bit
command: gmake -C c colibri CC=gcc (baseline) or gmake -C c colibri (trial: clang); cp <history> <model>/.coli_usage; env DIRECT=1 PIPE=1 python3 coli run --model <model> --ngen 64 --temp 0 "Explain what a hash table is.". Three rounds, gcc then clang in each, one script. The commit is risner-main in github.com/risner/colibri: v2.1.0 plus the FreeBSD fixes now in dev, plus this PR's two commits.

hardware.cpu: 2x Intel Xeon Gold 6230 (40 cores, hyper-threading off, AVX-512 VNNI), Cisco UCS C240 M5, no GPU
hardware.storage: two NVMe drives on PCIe x2 links, striped with gstripe, UFS, about 2.6 GB/s sequential; the engine reads with O_DIRECT
hardware.os: FreeBSD 15.1 amd64; FreeBSD clang 19.1.7 and its libomp from the base system; gcc 14.2.0 (FreeBSD Ports Collection) and its libgomp from packages

config.hot_thread_tuning: on (engine default); KMP_BLOCKTIME=0 set by the engine on FreeBSD, read by libomp, ignored by libgomp
config.expert_usage_history: the same .coli_usage file copied back before every run, so every run pins the same experts (about 365 GB)
config.scenario: new process per run; decode of 64 tokens with every expert already in RAM (hit rate 100%)

quality.method: all six runs print the same 64 tokens (md5 of the generated text 8cb06830df75); gmake -C c check on FreeBSD 15.1 built with clang: 3112 tests OK, run at 890a7e3a, one commit before the KMP_BLOCKTIME line
